paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computational Insurance and Actuarial Science

summary: The paper presents three gate-based quantum insurance demonstrations: a numerical excess-evaluation algorithm using n+2 qubits, a 6-qubit superconducting-device reinsurance allocation experiment on Wukong with 3 RBS layers, and a 4-qubit variational QSVD for a 4x4 Lee-Carter mortality matrix over 200 optimization steps. The reported results show algorithmic feasibility and decreasing loss/divergence, but no practical quantum advantage over classical methods is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Numerical quantum excess evaluation for the policy excess problem, estimating expected payment E[max(0, X-M(X))] for a lognormal loss distribution using a gate-based quantum circuit.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n qubits encode N=2^n discretized loss values |j>; interval [0,10] is rescaled to [0,2^n-1] so basis state |x> represents 10x/(2^n-1).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected excess payment E[max(0, X-M(X))] = ∫ f(x)(x-M(x))dx, approximated by truncated and discretized sums.

problem_instance.description: Policy excess payment under a lognormal claim-size model with threshold function M(x).

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic lognormal distribution with mu=0, sigma=1; numerical truncation over x∈[0,10].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate integral to [0,10]; discretize into N=2^n points; normalize probabilities pj=f(Xj)/C.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Numerical simulation comparing R_theory, R_truncate, and R_discrete as qubit number n increases.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare distribution state UX; compute truncated/discretized reference values.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure auxiliary qubit and use probability relation to recover expected payment.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: State preparation plus controlled rotations on n+2 qubits; no hardware benchmark or classical runtime comparison reported.
limiting_factors: No physical QPU experiment reported for the excess-evaluation algorithm
Only numerical simulation results are shown
State preparation of a general distribution is a major bottleneck

notes: No physical QPU is named for the excess-evaluation numerical study; QPanda is mentioned as the framework, so hardware is inferred as simulator_other.
The paper states the algorithm uses n+2 qubits, but n is varied and no concrete n is fixed in the text, so total num_qubits is not directly reported.
The paper describes the circuit structure (state preparation, subtractor, controlled rotations) but does not give a numeric depth.
No asymptotic complexity comparison is provided for this experiment.
The paper presents a numerical gate-based algorithm for policy excess evaluation and does not claim demonstrated practical advantage.

experiments.description: Experimental variational quantum optimization for reinsurance type allocation on the superconducting processor Wukong, minimizing portfolio variance under a fixed allocation constraint.

algorithm.variant: variational quantum optimization with problem-specified ansatz and RBS layers
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized initialization layer + repeated reconfigurable Beam Splitter (RBS) gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: iterative optimization until loss decreases toward target; 60 iterations shown
algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameterized initialization layer chosen to satisfy the allocation constraint; specific parameter values not reported.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variable x_j∈{0,1} indicates whether retained risk R_j is self-managed; 6-qubit circuit used in the experiment.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x Var[R_total] = x^T V x subject to sum_j x_j = pn, where R_total = Σ_j x_j R_j.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraint enforced by a problem-specified ansatz that preserves the fixed Hamming-weight subspace; no penalty function used.

problem_instance.description: Reinsurance type allocation over a portfolio of insurance products with fixed allocation proportion.

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated covariance matrix V; retained risks R_j can be vectors of historical data or random variables from stochastic simulation, but the experiment uses randomly generated covariance matrix.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Covariance matrix randomly generated; constraint-preserving ansatz used; noisy shots filtered via measurement-based mitigation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Loss function tracked over 60 iterations; quantum output compared with classically computed loss using same parameters ('quantum classical') and target value.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random covariance matrix generation; construction of cost Hamiltonian; constraint-preserving ansatz design.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Exclude erroneous shots using calibration-based reverse operation; compute noiseless loss classically for benchmarking.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 6 superconducting qubits on Wukong, 3 RBS layers, measurement-based error mitigation, classical optimizer loop.
limiting_factors: Only 6 qubits, far below practical advantage scale
No asymptotic speedup or crossover analysis
No evidence of outperforming classical optimization

notes: The paper explicitly states 6 superconducting qubits on Wukong.
The ansatz is described as 3 RBS layers, but no numeric circuit depth is given; depth is therefore not directly reported.
The paper does not provide an asymptotic speedup analysis for this experiment.
The paper reports decreasing loss on the quantum device and a classical recomputation of the same parameters, but no demonstrated quantum advantage over classical optimization.

experiments.description: Experimental quantum singular value decomposition / variational QSVD for the Lee-Carter mortality forecasting model using real mortality data on the superconducting processor Wukong.

algorithm.variant: variational QSVD for Lee-Carter mortality forecasting
algorithm.ansatz: two parameterized quantum circuits UA(θ1) and VB(θ2)

hyperparameters.loss_function: shot-wise equality loss C = (1/Nm) Σ δ(px,qx)

algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameters optimized on the quantum computer; initial values not reported.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Real-world mortality matrix D of size 4x4 is vectorized and encoded into a bipartite quantum state for QSVD.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate left and right singular vectors β_x and κ_t of D in the Lee-Carter model; minimize loss between measured bitstrings from the two subsystems.

problem_instance.description: Lee-Carter mortality forecasting on real mortality data from mortality.org, years 2014-2017 and ages 0-10/14, reduced to a 4x4 matrix.

dataset_specification.description: Real-world mortality data; years 2014-2017; age range 0 to 10-14; matrix D set to 4x4.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Construct D with elements D_{x,t}=ln m_{x,t}-α_x; perform SVD target extraction of β_x and κ_t.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Track loss function over 200 optimization steps; report Frobenius norm distance ||D-βκ||_F and K-L divergences D_KL(β||β_x), D_KL(κ||κ_t).

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct D from mortality data; compute α_x and target singular vectors; prepare bipartite state for QSVD.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use optimized parameters to benchmark Frobenius norm and K-L divergences against theoretical singular vectors.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4 superconducting qubits on Wukong, variational QSVD with 200 optimization steps, classical optimizer, real mortality data.
limiting_factors: Only a 4x4 matrix and 4 qubits are used
No classical runtime or accuracy baseline is reported
Hybrid variational loop depends on classical optimization
Data loading and state preparation remain nontrivial

notes: The paper explicitly states 4 superconducting qubits on Wukong and 200 optimization steps.
No numeric circuit depth or gate counts are reported.
The paper does not provide an asymptotic speedup analysis for the QSVD experiment.
The paper reports successful optimization of the Lee-Carter QSVD on Wukong, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.
